defaults.PANTHEON_BFF_HEALTH_RECOVERY_SUCCESSES: 3 consecutive OK probes, so one lucky probe cannot close an incident
defaults.PANTHEON_BFF_HEALTH_RECOVERY_MIN_SECONDS: 120s span between first and last of those OK probes (4+ probes at the 30s interval), so a burst of fast OKs is not recovery
defaults.PANTHEON_BFF_HEALTH_REOPEN_WINDOW_SECOND: 600s hold after sustained recovery before resolve is queued; covers the observed 5 to 15 minute flap period. A failure inside the hold keeps the same incident (the failure clears recovery progress); a failure after the resolve opens a new incident

mechanism: incident_recovery table (one row per target) tracks the OK streak; resolve is queued only when the streak, span and hold are all met. No incidents-service change: the incident stays open during the hold instead of being resolved then reopened, so no extra postmortem draft is created.
continuous_outage: unchanged: open after the existing failure threshold (3), one incident; test_continuous_outage_opens_exactly_one_at_threshold
error_rate_path: _queue_error_rate_window_sync uses the same reserve_incident: an opening/open incident is continued (and recovery progress cleared), a new incident is only created after resolve, so it follows the same hold and cannot flap inside it
evolution_journal: evolution_journal_auto_proposal_counts total no longer includes postmortem drafts; postmortem_draft is a separate labelled count; the auto_proposals list still shows drafts. Tests: test_bff_b3_evolution_journal.py and test_evolution_router.py updated
not_changed: existing incidents and postmortem drafts are not deleted or rewritten

runtime_budget.after: one incident and one draft per outage; per target at most one per (recovery span + 600s) in the worst alternating case; expected single digits per day. Not yet re-measured on hosted (needs a deploy)
